chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from his brother Al-Hasan from Zur'ah from Sama'ah said:

I asked him (peace be upon him) about a man who divorced his wife while he was ill. He said: She inherits him as long as she is in her waiting period. And if he divorced her in a state of harm (delaying the final pronouncement), she does not inherit him until a year. If one day is added to the year, she does not inherit him, and she observes a waiting period of four months and ten days, which is the waiting period of the one whose husband has died.

key_terms.إِضْرَار: Harm / Delay (in the context of revocable divorce)

ai.seo_question: How does a husband's illness affect his wife's inheritance and waiting period upon divorce?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfabar clarifies the distinction between a divorce pronounced during illness (which carries the presumption of death, 'marad al-mawt') and a standard divorce, specifically regarding the wife's inheritance duration. It establishes that if the husband dies after a year has passed since the divorce, the wife transitions from inheriting as a divorced spouse to inheriting as a widow, observing the four months and ten days 'iddah. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential view that illness serves as a bridge between life and death, affecting both marital status and inheritance rights.
